tweet_summary: A high-follower partisan account frames Minnesota's voter 'vouching' law as 'voter fraud': says a registered voter can vouch for 8 others with 'No ID required. No proof of residency.' Implies systemic fraud.
why_note_decision: The tweet mixes a true detail (one voter may vouch for up to eight others in their precinct) with a misleading omission ('No ID required'). Under Minn. Stat. 201.061, the person being vouched for STILL must provide their MN driver's license/ID number OR the last four digits of their SSN to verify identity; vouching only substitutes for proof of residency, not for identity verification. Calling this 'voter fraud' on a 2.9M-impression tweet implying a structural exploit warrants a note that supplies the missing identity-verification fact and the historic context (50+ year-old law). The original note merely restated the law without correcting 'No ID required,' which is why raters tagged it noteNotNeeded + missingKeyPoints.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note corrects the tweet's 'No ID required' claim — the registrant must still provide a MN ID/driver's-license number or last 4 of SSN for identity verification; vouching substitutes only for proof of residency. The note need not restate the (true) detail that one voter may vouch for up to eight others, though doing so adds context. FAIL notes that just restate the law without addressing the 'no ID' misframing. Bonus: note that the law is 50+ years old, and that the voucher signs an oath under penalty of perjury.
reference_note: Minnesota law (Minn. Stat. 201.061) lets a registered precinct voter vouch for up to eight others, but ONLY as proof of residency. The voter still must supply a MN ID/driver's license number or last 4 of SSN for identity verification, and the voucher signs an oath under penalty of perjury. Vouching has existed for 50+ years. https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/201.061 https://www.sos.mn.gov/elections-voting/register-to-vote/register-on-election-day/

original_unhelpful_note.text: Vouching is a legal same-day registration process in Minnesota where a registered precinct voter can vouch for up to eight others per election day by signing an oath attesting to their residency. https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/201.061 https://www.sos.mn.gov/elections-voting/register-to-vote/register-on-election-day/
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: missing_key_points: restates the law without correcting the tweet's 'No ID required' misframing — the registrant still must provide MN ID/SSN for identity, vouching substitutes only for residency proof

fact_check.notes: Vouching is real (up to 8 per registered precinct voter) and has existed 50+ years. 'No ID required' is wrong — the registrant must provide MN ID/driver's-license number or last 4 of SSN. The voucher signs an oath under penalty of perjury.

importance.lens_rationale: Election-integrity claims with millions of impressions feed into long-term democratic-discourse trust; correcting the 'no ID required' framing is meaningful for civic infrastructure.
